task.title: Trimming audio
task.shortdesc: Remove silence, false starts and mistakes by selecting a region of the waveform and deleting it.

context.p: Trimming removes unwanted audio from the start, end or middle of a track. When you delete a region, the audio on either side closes the gap.
context.note: Zoom in with Ctrl+1 to make precise selections; zoom back out with Ctrl+3.

step.cmd: Click and drag in the waveform to select the region you want to remove.

info.p: The selected region is highlighted. To select the whole track, press Ctrl+A (Windows and Linux) or Cmd+A (macOS).

info.note: Deleting changes the audio in the project. Undo with Ctrl+Z if you removed the wrong region.

step.cmd: To keep only the selection and discard everything else, choose EditRemove SpecialTrim Audio instead.
Play the track from just before the edit to check the join sounds natural.

info.p: If you hear a click at the join, select a few milliseconds around it and apply EffectFade In or Fade Out.

step.cmd: Save the project with FileSave ProjectSave Project.

info.p: Audacity saves the project as a single .aup3 file in the folder you choose; the Save Project dialog suggests your Documents folder.

result.p: The unwanted audio is gone and the track plays through without a gap.
